name: Citizenship by Merit

qualifying_event.description: Malta's Minister responsible for citizenship may grant citizenship to a person judged to have made an exceptional contribution to Malta or to humanity (e.g. in science, technology/innovation, culture and the arts, sport, entrepreneurship, philanthropy, or public service), under Subsidiary Legislation 188.04 of 2017, revisited in 2025 after the European Court of Justice ruled against Malta's former investment-based citizenship framework.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: None published. Assessed case-by-case at ministerial discretion; the administering agency states it does not permit marketing or promotion of this legislation.

requirements.blocker_text: No published eligibility criteria, thresholds, or standard application procedure exist for this route. Grants are discretionary and assessed strictly on a case-by-case basis; the administering agency explicitly states this is 'neither a programme nor a scheme, pathway, continuation, or alternative' to Malta's former investment-citizenship framework, and that it does not permit marketing or promotion of the underlying legislation.

sources.title: Agenzija Komunita Malta -- Citizenship by Merit: confirms the route is discretionary, is not a programme/scheme, derives from SL 188.04 (2017) as revisited after the 2025 ECJ ruling, and states the Agency does not permit marketing of this legislation

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Malta's initial build. INCLUDED FOR LEGAL COMPLETENESS ONLY -- this is NOT a practically accessible immigration pathway for an ordinary applicant. Confirmed directly at tier-1, but the source itself discloses no income, investment, contribution, or residence thresholds, and explicitly declines to characterise this as a programme at all. Kept as status:'draft' because there is nothing beyond the bare existence of the mechanism to validate against; this may remain permanently under-specified by design given the Agency's anti-marketing stance, rather than pending future disclosure. CLEARLY DISTINCT from Malta's former Citizenship by Naturalisation for Exceptional Services by Direct Investment (CES/MEIN) programme, which required an investment of roughly EUR600,000-750,000 plus qualifying property and 12-36 months of residence: CES was abolished by Act XXI of 2025 following an April 2025 European Court of Justice ruling that citizenship-for-investment lacked 'a genuine link between a country and its citizens' in violation of EU law. CES is NOT modelled as an active route in this dataset since it no longer accepts applicants; Citizenship by Merit is its legal (not practical) successor context, per tier-1 and corroborating tier-3/tier-4 commentary (e.g. Global Citizen Solutions, imin-malta.com).
